articles.title: Hideo Kojima responds to accusations of Physint being over budget and late on deadline, says he still "loves Sony" despite collapse of publishing deal
articles.summary: Last week, we learned that Sony "stepped away" from Kojima Production's previously PlayStation-exclusive "action espionage" game Physint. Following the announcement, which saw Xbox take over publishing duties for the in-development title, a new report has claimed Sony's decision was the result of…
body: Now, IGN has conducted an interview with Kojima that sheds a little more light on the situation. In the chat - which covers a range of topics including Kojima's fears for the future of the studio, the perils of working on multiple projects at once, and the implications of losing Sony resources - Kojima detailed how the conversation with the platform holder went, noting how that he was in a state of shock at the time, and finds the meeting difficult to recall.

"I don't remember so much of that meeting, to be honest with you," Kojima told IGN. "And my colleagues probably don't remember as well, so I can't really answer if you ask me what exactly they said. But, from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry.

"Nothing could've prepared me for their decision to step away from the project. So I thought, "What am I going to do from tomorrow?" But from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry."

articles.title: Disney Plus Just Proved You Won't Be Able to Escape Ads On Any Tier
articles.summary: Disney Plus has updated its subscriber agreement, and it's not looking good for Premium subscribers. The subscriber agreement now states that ads and promotional content can play for subscribers, regardless of their Disney Plus tier.
body: It may be tempting to bypass ads with an ad blocker, but Disney reaffirms that it can suspend or terminate the user's subscription and prevent streaming while the ad blocker is enabled. Disney can even increase an ad blocker user's subscription tier to Disney Plus Premium, as it offers "the most similar features or functionality" to using Disney Plus with an ad blocker, and bill the new price from the date of the move.

At this point, the only accounts that are not subject to ads are Junior Mode accounts. Basic Disney Plus costs $11.99 a month with ads, while Premium costs $18.99 monthly. Premium users pay an additional $7 to avoid ads, but now even that extra money may not be enough to guarantee they are kept away from unwanted ads.

Not so long ago, it was suggested that Disney Plus could make the service free in exchange for users watching ads. However, it seems that Disney is headed in a direction where users will keep paying, the subscription will get increasingly expensive, and they may still end up watching ads anyway.

articles.title: Kojima Productions Confirms The Studio Is Alright After Concerning Physint Report
articles.summary: Following reporting about the rocky development of Physint, Kojima Productions stated the studio is in a "healthy, profitable state" on X. Kojima Productions is also asking players to take any unofficial statements about Physint's publisher switch "with a dose of scepticism," although it doesn't…
body: On Sept. 9, we learned that PlayStation would no longer publish Physint and that Xbox would now publish the game. On Sept. 11, Bloomberg reported on why the publisher switch happened, revealing that PlayStation dropped the project because Kojima Productions missed deadlines and the Death Stranding games hadn't been very profitable for Sony. Now, in a lengthy statement on X, Kojima Productions has responded.

"None of the claims written came from any official or on-the-record source and as such we encourage you to take them with a dose of scepticism," the X post explains. "Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications. While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong."

articles.title: Wit Studio President George Wada Is Ready to Bring One Piece to a New Generation
articles.summary: With over 1190 chapters of the manga and 1170 episodes of its first (and still ongoing) anime adaptation from Toei Animation, One Piece has built an impressive world with hundreds of characters and locations, and deep lore spanning almost a millennium of history.
body: Wit Studio has built its stellar reputation over the past 15 years with popular series like Attack on Titan, Vinland Saga, and Spy x Family. These anime all garnered international success and praise, but the Japanese studio now faces perhaps its biggest challenge: bringing another masterpiece manga to the screen as an anime remake: One Piece.
Wit Studio president Joji "George" Wada is well aware of the magnitude of this endeavor. Speaking to Polygon via email, Wada describes One Piece as “a treasure Japan can be proud of.”

The first seven episodes of the remake, titled The One Piece, will begin airing on Netflix in February 2027. They will depict the beginning of Luffy’s journey in the East Blue, adapting the first 50 chapters of Eiichiro Oda’s manga, but Wada suggested that the studio is taking a holistic approach.

“We have deeply absorbed the vast world of One Piece from its enormous body of source material,” Wada says. “Carrying that world with us, our task was to depict the opening of a new voyage all over again, with all of its heart-racing excitement.”

articles.title: Resident Evil and Silent Hill Are Just as Cozy as Animal Crossing, According to Science
articles.summary: You can feel it in the air, can’t you? We’re in the last couple weeks of summer, and spooky season is just around the corner. Zach Cregger’s new Resident Evil movie is getting rave reviews — including from us! So long swimming pools and barbecues, the people demand thrills and chills.
body: To learn more about the appeal of cozy horror, I spoke with affective neuroscientist Dr. Eric Leonardis, who’s an expert in how our brains process emotions through play and entertainment. (He previously weighed in on one of our most-anticipated fall games, Virtue and a Sledgehammer.) In the eyes of the good doctor, it’s all about taking back control.

“It's what they call dark play in the [neuroscientific] literature, this idea that if you have these explorations of negative themes, sometimes doing so will actually make you feel like you have more control over what might happen in the future,” Leonardis explained. “Because we've simulated it, we've thought it through, right? The classic example is like when Michael Myers comes up the stairs, and you're like, don't go into the basement, go out the front door. Get out of there. You know what I mean? This is what I would do in this situation, right? And that can be comforting.”
He adds that horror can feel cozy because we know we are safe in the heat of the moment, even if our character is getting their neck ripped open by a vicious zombie.

articles.title: The latest co-op indie game to take over the internet is like one of my favourite board games, just with bombs
articles.summary: They say if you give a monkey an infinite amount of time to randomly hit keys on a typewriter it will almost surely write Shakespeare's complete works, word for word. But what happens when you give three monkeys with restricted access to their senses a limited amount of time to defuse a bomb?
body: This is the terrifying reality you must face in Bombanana, the new co-op bomb disposal game where you and three friends play as monkeys. The monkey part is fun, but not as crucial to the set up as the fact that one of you can't see, one can't hear, and one can't speak; that really throws a spanner in the works. It's like Team 3, the co-op building game which is also based on the three wise monkeys.
I rounded up some friends and started as the monkey who can't see, who also happens to be the monkey that has to defuse the bomb. It's as tricky as you'd expect.

None of us had any clue what was going on or how to communicate with one another. The person who had the instruction manual couldn't speak, the only person who could see what they were doing couldn't hear instructions or questions, and I couldn't see what the hell was going on—plus I'm pretty bad under pressure. In the end we just sat back, threw bananas at each other, and waited for the bomb to put us all out of our misery so we could regroup, strategise, and try again.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima says he was 'shocked' after Sony cut ties with Physint over a Zoom call: 'Nothing could’ve prepared me for their decision to step away from the project'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Sony's recent decision to cut ties with Kojima Productions's Physint is one of the more unexpected turns of 2026. Even with the industry's many struggles, and speculation that Death Stranding 2 didn't sell as well as Sony hoped, the PlayStation studio shutting the door on one of the industry's most famed and respected designers was a huge surprise.

While Kojima Productions would eventually find a new publisher for Physint in Microsoft, it took a frantic three months of pitching for that happen. This is partly because Kojima himself was similarly blindsided by Sony's decision, as the veteran designer revealed in the first interview he's given since switching publishers.

Speaking to IGN, Kojima revealed that in June, Sony contacted him saying they wanted to have a Zoom call, which he agreed to. It was during that call when Sony broke the bad news: "They said they can no longer fund development for Physint. I was shocked and I said 'What did you say?'" Kojima explained. "I couldn't quite process what they had said. I wasn't sure because I was in such shock."
points: Sony's recent decision to cut ties with Kojima Productions's Physint is one of the more unexpected turns of 2026.

articles.title: I urge you to check out this hidden object game where you play as the world's most helpful sniper
articles.summary: On the list of activities that could feasibly be described as "wholesome", sniping is probably close to the bottom. While I enjoy ventilating skulls from improbably long distances in games like Battlefield 6 and Wardogs, it wouldn't be the first activity that I would consider sharing with the…
body: Which is why I so admire Sniper Dan 's attempt to turn sharpshooting into a positive experience on both sides of the scope. Developed by Autonauts creators Denki, Sniper Dan smashes together hidden-object games and first-person shooting, and in doing so produces a surprisingly effective symbiotic relationship.

The loose premise sees Dan—a crack-shot armed with a hunting rifle and an entrepreneurial spirit, venture out into his local community hellbent upon projectile-based problem solving. Each mission is like a 3D, animated wimmelbilderbuch, scattered with dozens of people, animals, and inanimate objects which may or may not require bullet-based assistance.

In play, Sniper Dan couldn't be simpler. You spy a problem, shoot the problem, and solve the problem. What makes it interesting is the wacky array of problems that require your assistance. You might be asked to help blow away piles of leaves in the local park, open a jammed suitcase by shooting the lock, or plant a seed by blasting it into the ground, shooting the pile of soil to cover it, and puncturing the watering can to ensure the soil is sufficiently doused.

articles.title: Tokyo Walled City looks set to fill the Deus Ex-shaped hole in my life
articles.summary: It's been more than a decade since the last Deus Ex game, and it's unlikely we'll see another one any time soon. Yet while Adam Jensen's story remains frustratingly unfinished thanks to the cliffhanger ending of Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, the indie scene has offered fresh hope for fans of sneaking…
body: Unveiled at TGS 2026, Tokyo Walled City is described by developer Grim Ronin as a "stealth action retro-cyberpunk immersive sim with survival horror and RPG elements". So, Deus Ex with scary bits, basically. You play as Reiko Kimura, a mercenary who is trapped in a dense, fortified district of Japan's capital, the name of which implies it is inspired by the Internet's favourite historic enclave Kowloon Walled City. Blade Runner is another clear inspiration, with the opening shot of the game's trailer showing a cityscape that directly references Blade Runner's "Coke billboard" scene.

The rest of the trailer offers a montage of all the classic immersive sim tropes. Vent crawling, disabling security cameras, hacking into computers, 0451, shooting out lights, leaning around corners. But TWC isn't a straight Deus Ex knockoff. There are shades of Dishonored in here too. Reiko is considerably nimbler than JC Denton, able to skip across rooftops with ease and perform drop assassinations with a blade.
points: It's been more than a decade since the last Deus Ex game, and it's unlikely we'll see another one any time soon.

articles.title: Big Bang Theory Spinoff Features Surprise Live-Action Cameos from The Flash and Mr. Freeze
articles.summary: Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe featured a surprise fight between a live-action Flash and Mr. Freeze, but the show's creators originally wanted a different DC hero cameo.
body: Fans of the sci-fi comedy offshoot may have been surprised to see it dive headfirst into comic book crossover territory when Season 1 Episode 9 premiered earlier this week. The episode saw Stuart Bloom and his universe-traveling companions plopped into a Gotham City come to life, with things quickly taking a turn when none other than classic Batman villain Mr. Freeze (played here by Eric Allan Kramer) shows up.

TV show budgets aside, this is a full-on live-action take on Victor Fries that shoots killer icicles, builds giant ice walls, and even tries to kill Stuart with a giant icy bowling ball. DC fans found even more to recognize when a live-action version of Jay Garrick's Flash (played by Andy Ridings) ran in to save the day – and deliver a few one-liners.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe packed in the references, with there even being a mention that Golden Age Flash should probably be fighting someone like Captain Cold instead of Mr. Freeze. It was enough to get tongues wagging on social media, with fans mostly just happy to see any live-action Flash for the first time since Ezra Miller played Barry Allen in 2023's universe-ending standalone film.
points: Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe featured a surprise fight between a live-action Flash and Mr. Freeze, but the show's creators originally wanted a different DC hero cameo.

articles.title: The Last of Us Director Apologizes to God of War Laufey Devs After Calling Recent AAA Games 'Boring'
articles.summary: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."
body: The comments in question surfaced as part of a recently published piece by Edge magazine and saw the former Naughty Dog developer tackling the state of AAA gaming and game development. Straley initially said with a laugh that he thinks "the verbs and experiences we're delivering in the triple-A space are… I wanna say boring," before bringing God of War Laufey into the equation.

"God of War Laufey, I look at that game, and every pixel is mindblowing," he said to Edge. "The amount of work and skill that's gone into every single frame… I've made those kinds of games, and I'm still blown away. But when I actually look at what you're doing in the game? I'm not excited. And that's nothing against the God of War team. Just, across the board in triple-A, it feels like there’s no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas."

The Last of Us has certainly had its influence on the state of big-budget games, so it was no surprise to see social media light up with reactions to Straley's thoughts. The former Naughty Dog lead then followed up the commotion with a thread of posts on X/Twitter, taking the opportunity to elaborate on his perspective on where the industry is at and where it's heading.
points: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."

body: In this video, hosted by Marc 'Try4ce' Duddleson, we take an in-depth look at Final Fantasy 14, running on the Nintendo Switch 2. We analyse its 720p handheld and 1080p docked performance, 30fps target, and image quality settings. How does it stack up against other platforms? We compare Switch 2 directly to Xbox Series S, PS4, PS5, Series X, and PC handhelds like the Steam Deck, breaking down anti-aliasing, visual features, load times, and subscription model quirks.

videos.title: Absolum - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition – Launch Trailer
videos.summary: Play Absolum - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition now:
body: Play as the outcast heroes of Talamh, explore dangerous lands, battle brutal bosses, unlock powerful upgrades, and uncover the mystery of Azra's absolute magical power!

Absolum - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition runs at 60 fps for smoother gameplay, has improved resolution, and lets you play with Gameshare locally. Nintendo Switch players will be able to upgrade to the Switch 2 version for free while keeping their earned progression and saved games!
Will you defy the Sun King and change the fate of this world?
